commit_message:
[wasm] Introduce WasmModuleSignatureStorage

This replaces a Zone we used for storing signatures, array types, and
struct types. Zones are meant for temporary storage and are not very
memory efficient.

The new WasmModuleSignatureStorage provides pointer stability and a
similar interface than a zone, but has less memory overhead.

R=jkummerow@chromium.org

findings.title: Unsynchronized read of WasmModuleSignatureStorage in EstimateStoredSize/EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption
findings.message: WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize() reads `signature_storage.TotalReservedSize()` (and the aggregate `WasmModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` which calls EstimateStoredSize()) without acquiring any lock. However, `signature_storage` (introduced in this commit, replacing the former `signature_zone`) is `mutable` and is concurrently mutated during instantiation (e.g. when fast API call signatures are added) while protected by `NativeModule::allocation_mutex_` elsewhere in the codebase. `NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` in wasm-code-manager.cc calls `module_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` at the very top of the function, before acquiring `allocation_mutex_` (the mutex is only taken later, around the `owned_code_`/`new_owned_code_`/`debug_info_` bookkeeping). Because the memory-consumption estimation can run concurrently (e.g. from `d8`'s performance.measureMemory or background profiling) with module instantiation on another thread that appends to `signature_storage`, this is a data race (TOCTOU/missing synchronization) on the underlying `std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>> storage_` backing store, which can corrupt the vector's internal size/capacity bookkeeping or allow a torn read, leading to incorrect memory accounting and, under race conditions on reallocation, potential use of stale/invalid pointers or crashes. The original Zone-based implementation (`signature_zone.allocation_size_for_tracing()`) had the same unprotected access pattern, but the comment on the class explicitly acknowledges concurrent mutation during instantiation is expected, making the omission of locking in the size-estimation path a clear oversight.

location.snippet:
size_t WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize() const {
  UPDATE_WHEN_CLASS_CHANGES(WasmModule,
#if V8_ENABLE_DRUMBRAKE
                            912
#else   // V8_ENABLE_DRUMBRAKE
                            880
#endif  // V8_ENABLE_DRUMBRAKE
  );
  return sizeof(WasmModule) +                            // --
         signature_storage.TotalReservedSize() +         // --
         ContentSize(types) +                            // --

findings.suggestion: Protect all accesses to `signature_storage` (both reads from EstimateStoredSize/EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption and writes during instantiation) with `NativeModule::allocation_mutex_`. In NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption(), acquire the allocation_mutex_ before calling `module_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` (which transitively reads signature_storage), and only release it after that call completes but before calling into `debug_info_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` to avoid a lock-order inversion with WasmScript::SetBreakPointForFunction. Also move `signature_storage.TotalReservedSize()` out of EstimateStoredSize() into EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption() so it is always evaluated under the lock.

ground_truth.root_cause: When `signature_zone` (a Zone) was replaced by the custom `WasmModuleSignatureStorage` class in commit b9068d13bb1, the new class's `TotalReservedSize()` accessor was invoked from `WasmModule::EstimateStoredSize()`/`EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` exactly as the old Zone accessor had been — i.e., without any synchronization — even though the class's own doc comment states that `signature_storage` is mutated during instantiation on a `const WasmModule`. The call chain `NativeModule::EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` → `module_->EstimateCurrentMemoryConsumption()` executes before `NativeModule::allocation_mutex_` is acquired in that function, so a concurrent instantiation thread appending to `signature_storage` races with the reading thread.
